title: Your masjid and your people
hook: There's only one first visit. After that, it's just your masjid.

screens.text: A week ago you said your shahada. Today: walking into **{{masjid.name}}** without feeling lost, praying in a row, and meeting the people who'll walk this road with you.
The **masjid** (mosque) is where Muslims pray together. Tap each part to see what to expect.

areas.entrance: Many masjids have a separate entrance for each gender. If you're unsure where to go, ask anyone.
areas.shoes: **Shoes off** at the entrance. There's usually a shelf.
areas.wudu: Every masjid has a place to make wudu. Arriving with wudu already helps.
areas.hall: People **sit on the floor**; chairs are mostly for older or unwell people. Dress **modestly and loosely**.{women} Bring a scarf: you cover your hair to pray.{/women}
areas.women: {women}Your space: rows behind the men, or an area of your own. If you're unsure, ask anyone.{/women}{men}The sisters' prayer space: rows behind the men's, or an area of their own.{/men}

cards.back: Maybe. Most will be glad. You can simply say, "I'm new, could you show me where to go?"
Everyone did, once. If someone corrects you rudely, that's on them, not you. Mention it to {{mentor.name}}.
Any prayer time works. Maghrib and Isha are often calm. Friday's Jumu'ah prayer is the busiest (Day 11).
The imam leads the prayer and teaches. You can talk to him about anything, privately.

screens.text: **Praying in a row.** One person, the **imam**, leads; everyone else lines up behind him. The Prophet ﷺ said the imam is there to be followed [Bukhari 734].
bubbles: His Companions stood **shoulder to shoulder, feet beside feet**, in straight rows [Bukhari 725].
{women}Women pray in rows behind the men, or in their own area.{/women}

screens.title: Following the imam
screens.intro: Stay a beat behind him the whole way. Never go ahead of him [Bukhari 734].

moves.text: Line up shoulder to shoulder. In your heart, intend to pray behind the imam.
Stand while he recites. {{masjid.name}} will show you whether to recite al-Fatiha quietly behind him.
Bow just after he bows. Say your *Subhan Allah* quietly.
Prostrate just after he prostrates. Never go ahead of him.
End with the salam after he does.

screens.prompt: You're joining a prayer at the masjid. Put these in order.
items: Line up shoulder to shoulder in the row
Intend to pray behind the imam
Say Allahu akbar after he says it
Stand behind him while he recites
Bow and prostrate just after him
Say the salam after he does
screens.feedback: That's it. Just stay a beat behind him the whole way, and you can't go wrong.

screens.text: **Arrived late?** For now, you can wait quietly and pray on your own once they finish, or join and ask someone to show you how to complete what you missed. Day 22 teaches it.
Fill the row in front before starting a new one. Tap the spot you'd take.

screens.situation: After Isha, Hannah is putting on her shoes. A woman she doesn't know says, "You're new! Welcome. We have a sisters' circle on Thursdays."

options.text: Smile, say thanks, and ask what time it starts
options.feedback: Yes. That one small yes is how most converts find their people.

options.text: Say thanks and leave quickly; she's not ready for groups
options.feedback: Understandable, but you don't need to be ready. Showing up once, even quietly, is enough.

options.text: Explain she's still learning and might mess up
options.feedback: No need. Everyone there is still learning too. You'll be welcome as you are.

screens.text: **Your people.** Converts who have Muslim friends, feel at home in a masjid and know a good imam do best over time [Yaqeen 2025]. This app can teach you. It can't be your friend.
bubbles: So meet **{{mentor.name}}**. Ask questions, say when it's hard. That's what they're there for.

screens.prompt: One week in. What was the hardest moment so far, and what's one thing you're proud of? (Even "I prayed once" counts.)

chips: What should I wear to the masjid?
Can I go on my period?

screens.text: Visit {{masjid.name}}, or set up a time to meet {{mentor.name}}.
steps: Go for one prayer: shoes off, line up, follow the imam
Before you leave, say salam to one person
Or message {{mentor.name}} to set up a time to meet
screens.optional_extra: If you meet your mentor, tap "I met my mentor."

screens.text: Shoes off, sit on the floor, line up shoulder to shoulder, and follow the imam a beat behind. Then stay a few minutes and meet someone.
**Week one, done.** You said your shahada, learned wudu, prayed, and started finding your people. That's a lot.

check.prompt: Praying behind an imam, when do you bow?

options.feedback: Right. The imam is there to be followed, so you move a beat after him [Bukhari 734].

options.text: Whenever you're ready, at your own pace
options.feedback: Not quite. In a group, you follow the imam's timing, just after him [Bukhari 734].

check.prompt: How do people stand in the rows?

options.text: Shoulder to shoulder, in straight lines
options.feedback: Right. That's how the Companions lined up [Bukhari 725].

options.text: Spread out, with space between each person
options.feedback: Not quite. Rows are straight and close, shoulder to shoulder [Bukhari 725].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The imam is to be followed: say the takbir after him, bow after him, prostrate after him; never go ahead [Bukhari 734; First Instructions on Worship, praying in a group].
- Straight rows, shoulder to shoulder and foot beside foot [Bukhari 725]; women stand behind the men or in their own area [First Instructions on Worship].
- Hanafi: the follower doesn't recite al-Fatiha or a surah in any prayer, audible or silent; the imam's recitation suffices [Muslim 404; Q 7:204; Research Notes - Core Essentials, madhab table]. Tasbih in ruku' and sujud and the sitting words are still said quietly. On rising from bowing, the follower says only *Rabbana wa lakal-hamd* (Day 10).
- Congregation is twenty-seven times better than praying alone [Bukhari 645].
- Strongest predictors of good convert outcomes: religious Muslim friends, mosque attachment, a capable imam [Yaqeen 2025]. Being "criticized, frowned upon, or rudely corrected" at a mosque is a top turn-off for converts [ISPU RMS].
- Masjid basics: shoes off, floor seating, separate entrances, modest dress [Field Guide ch. 11; Welcome to Islam D3].

**Likely questions**
- *"What do I wear?"* Loose, opaque, covering clothes; women bring a scarf to cover hair for prayer. No need for special "Muslim clothes."
- *"Can I go on my period?"* Scholars differ on staying in the prayer hall; many masjids have areas she can use for classes and events. Defer to the masjid's practice.
- *"Joined late, what now?"* Simple: joining wherever the imam is is best (Day 22 shows how); praying alone after is allowed if they feel lost. Don't teach the full make-up procedure now.
- *"What do I say to the imam?"* "As-salamu 'alaykum, I'm new, I took my shahada recently." That's enough.
- *"Nobody talked to me."* Validate. Suggest staying after prayer, going to a class or event, and letting the mentor introduce them.
- *"Do I say al-Fatiha behind the imam?"* Masjid default Hanafi: no, stay silent and listen. Other schools differ (Madhab note).

**Escalate:** a convert who was mistreated or shamed at the masjid (pass to the imam with consent); safeguarding concerns with any adult (minors especially).

**Don't:** shame non-attendance; suggest they must go to every prayer; let them think a different school's practice they see is "wrong."
madhabNote: Behind the imam: Hanafis stay silent in every prayer. Malikis recite al-Fatiha quietly only in the silent prayers. Shafi'is recite it in every rak'ah, even behind the imam. Hanbalis recommend it in the silent prayers and in the imam's pauses. All four accept praying behind an imam of another school.
sourcesMd:
- [Bukhari 734](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:734): the imam is to be followed. [Bukhari 725](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:725): straight rows, shoulder to shoulder. [Bukhari 645](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:645): twenty-seven times.
- [Muslim 404](https://sunnah.com/muslim:404) and Qur'an [7:204](https://quran.com/7/204): silence while the Qur'an is recited (the Hanafi evidence for the follower's silence).
- First Instructions on Worship (Hanafi), praying in a group.
- The New Muslims Field Guide ch. 11 (the first masjid visit), ch. 12 (the company you keep). Welcome to Islam Day 3 (follow the imam), Day 5 (community).
- [ISPU, *Reimagining Muslim Spaces*](https://web.archive.org/web/2019/https://www.ispu.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/RMS_Creating-a-More-Welcoming-Mosque-for-Converts.pdf); [Yaqeen Institute, *Becoming Muslim* (2025)](https://yaqeeninstitute.org/read/data/reports/becoming-muslim-lives-of-american-converts-to-islam).
